what: is_land = land_frac >= land_threshold; the flag and water_type are both derived from it
meaning: Binary physical classification of a hex as land or ocean, at a configured area threshold (0.5).
note: land_fraction is stored alongside, so the underlying continuous quantity is never lost - only the binary view discards it.

what: classify_hexes returns land_class plus classification_error_area_m2 = np.where(is_land, water_area, land_area)
meaning: The project already NAMES the area thrown away by the binary decision, in both directions, including 'the land part of a water hex'.
note: This is the single strongest piece of evidence that the discarded coastal land is a known, quantified property of the physical model rather than an oversight.

what: documented: 'Binary class applies the threshold. Fractions are always preserved alongside the binary class.'
meaning: The binary/continuous split is deliberate and written down in the pipeline's own report text.
In the geography layer the flag is redefined as an alias of water_type, closing the loop with the threshold above.
note: Two definitions in two layers, but they agree: the audit found 0 hexes where is_terrestrial_hex disagreed with either land_fraction >= 0.5 or water_type == NONE.

what: water = layers['water_type'].to_numpy() != 'NONE' feeds the dominant terrain face
meaning: Terrain face is decided from the same binary class.
note: This is why reclassifying a 30 per cent land hex as LAND is not a free change: it would move terrain too.

what: the edge graph is purely geometric - corners, shared sides, river snapping - and reads neither is_terrestrial_hex nor water_type
meaning: There is currently NO movement layer consuming the flag.
note: Materially lowers the migration cost of any model that adds a political target type: there is no movement semantics to keep consistent yet.

what: 'Territorial targets are TERRESTRIAL_HEX (hex_id) or ISLAND_COMPONENT (component_id) ... and an OCEAN hex is never itself a land-control target.'
meaning: THE RULE IS EXPLICIT AND PREDATES THE ISLAND STAGES. It is a documented architectural invariant from MAPGEN-006R, not an accident of MAPGEN-021.
note: This single line decides the stage conclusion: the behaviour cannot be called a bug against intent, because the intent is written down.

meaning: Exactly two target types exist; there is no type for land that sits on an ocean hex but belongs to a landmass already represented elsewhere.

what: terr_hex = set(geo.loc[geo['is_terrestrial_hex'], 'hex_id']); every TERRESTRIAL_HEX control row must be in it or the scenario fails validation
meaning: This is the exact point where a PHYSICAL flag becomes a POLITICAL constraint, enforced by the canonical validator.
note: The coupling is enforced, not incidental. Any change of model has to pass through this check.

what: represented_by_terrestrial_hex = any(...); is_subhex_lost = bool(idx_list) and not represented_by_terrestrial_hex
meaning: A whole component that touches no terrestrial hex is flagged lost and becomes eligible for overlay and for an ISLAND_COMPONENT control target.
note: The escape hatch is per COMPONENT, not per hex - which is precisely why it cannot catch the coastal remainder of a component that IS represented.

what: check overlay_hexes_water_semantics_intact: all overlay hexes are non-terrestrial
meaning: Overlays live ON ocean hexes by design; the physical class is deliberately left alone.
note: Precedent that political representation can be added WITHOUT touching the water classification.

what: check no_duplicate_overlay_for_large_islands: a component already represented by a terrestrial hex must not also appear in an overlay unit
note: This is what blocks the naive reuse of the component mechanism for coastal fragments: Great Britain is represented by terrestrial hexes, so its coastal remainder may not be re-issued as an overlay component.
